Strait of Hormuz Status: October 15, 2026 | Straits Daily Brief

Strait of Hormuz · Daily brief · UTC
15 October 2026 .
Brent $ 105.73 -0.23 % · Transits 2 (2026-10-11) · AI-assisted
01 The New York Times reports cargo is floating in the Strait of Hormuz as Iranian shipping attacks continue to rise.

02 Bloomberg and CNN report a container ship sank in the strait after an attack; the UAE-managed GFS Pride, whose sinking India Shipping News reported, remains in the news cycle.

03 The Guardian reports at least six explosions struck near the presidential palace in Aden, with witnesses describing a Houthi missile strike on Saudi-led forces headquarters there.

Situation
Cargo is floating in the Strait of Hormuz as Iranian shipping attacks intensify, per The New York Times, Fox Business, ABC News, and Sky News. Bloomberg and CNN report that a container ship sank in the strait following an attack; Al Jazeera reports containers floating in the water after a vessel sank near the strait. The UAE-managed container ship GFS Pride, whose sinking near the strait India Shipping News reported, remains in the news cycle. IMF PortWatch recorded 2 transits on October 11, against a pre-crisis baseline of 85 per day. At the second front, The Guardian reports at least six explosions struck near the presidential palace in Aden used by Yemen's internationally recognized government, with witnesses reporting a Houthi missile strike on Saudi-led forces headquarters there. Fox Business reports that Iran has ramped up attacks on shipping in the strait. Brent stood at $105.73, down 0.23% over 24 hours, as of 20:59 UTC. This feed indexed 88 headlines in the past 24 hours. As of 21:22 UTC, 172 AIS-visible vessels were holding position away from berth in the Strait of Hormuz and Gulf watch box, a count that leaves out ships within 25km of a working port. On the Hormuz Index, Crisis Pressure, the state composite, sits in the extreme band, with its value set by physical transit deviation alone; the Escalation Forecast sits in the high band, with the Brent-WTI forward spread as its top contributor.
